achievements and so on, has been greater than our joy in
hearing the word of God? In short, is it not the case that we
are no longer ready to hear God's call and demand upon
our lives?
II
Someone, however, may be asking the question: "Yes, but
for what exactly should we be prepared? When did the
second invitation come to us: 'Come, for all is now ready'—
has it not been lacking?" This question leads us to remember
that whenever a nation as a whole turns away from the
Church, it is always individuals who are guilty of the
defection. It is the individual to whom the second invitation
is issued, the call: "Come, for all is now ready." And it
comes in fact just when he is not expecting it, when it is least
convenient, with the consequence that he prefers to close
his ears to it.
Just as at the time of Jesus it was His appearance itself
which embodied God's call-inconvenient and for the mass
of the people lost in the wind—so since those days, His call
has sounded everywhere and time and time again, as Jesus
Himself confronts us everywhere and time and time again.
Where does He meet us? Where have we failed to perceive
His presence or to hear His call? Jesus Himself has antici-
pated this question. To those who have failed to apprehend
His presence in life, the following words apply:
"I was hungry and you gave me no food, I was thirsty
and you gave me no drink, I was a stranger and you did not
welcome me, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in
prison and you did not visit me. Truly I say to you, as you
did it not to the least of these, you did it not to me" (Matt.
